id_and_class.summary: Kant holds that the world we consciously experience is a world of appearances, structured by the mind's own a priori forms: space and time as forms of intuition, and the categories of the understanding. Unified experience depends on the transcendental unity of apperception, the requirement that ‘I think’ can accompany all of one's representations, yet the self this presupposes is known only as it appears, never as a thinking substance.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Unifying Condition of Experience

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Kant does not say what consciousness is in itself. He identifies the conditions under which conscious experience of objects is possible, namely sensory matter given in space and time, synthesis by imagination and understanding, and the unity of apperception that lets representations belong to one subject.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Kant brackets the question. Mind and body alike are known only as appearances, and what either is in itself lies beyond knowledge. Within experience, his Refutation of Idealism argues that awareness of one's own existence in time presupposes perceiving persisting objects in space.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (Kant holds that the mind in itself is unknowable, so he gives no account of whether consciousness is fundamental or derived)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjectivity rests on the unity of apperception, since representations that could not be accompanied by ‘I think’ would be nothing to me. This ‘I’ is a formal, spontaneous act that tells me that I am but not what I am. Kant separates object-directed sensations from feelings such as pleasure and pain, which present only states of the subject.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Kant gives no theory of qualia. Sensation (Empfindung) supplies qualitative content such as color, sound, and warmth, and he assigns it an intensive magnitude, but he treats it mainly as matter awaiting synthesis and never asks why it feels as it does. His ‘phenomena’ are public objects of experience, not raw felt qualities.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Empirically real objects in space and time; things in themselves (noumena) that cannot be known; a priori forms of intuition and categories of the understanding contributed by the subject; a formal, non-substantial ‘I think’.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Transcendental argument, reasoning back from the fact of unified experience to its necessary conditions. Inner sense gives knowledge only of the self as it appears in time.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A manifold of sensory intuition given under space and time, concepts and categories such as substance and causality supplied by the understanding, the synthesis that combines them, and the unity of apperception that holds the whole together. In Kant's phrase, intuitions without concepts are blind and thoughts without intuitions are empty.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Unity of consciousness; self-consciousness; conditions of objective experience and cognition. Phenomenal character is presupposed, not explained.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The transcendental unity of apperception, the necessary possibility that ‘I think’ accompanies every representation, together with the active synthesis that brings sensory intuitions under concepts.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Experience is an active synthesis, never passive reception. The understanding continually combines the sensory manifold under its categories, and time, as the form of inner sense, orders every representation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Space is a form the subject imposes on outer appearances, so the constituting subject has no spatial location. Empirically, the self appears only as a sequence of states in inner sense.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness helps constitute the empirical world, since objects must conform to the mind's forms of cognition, a reversal Kant likened to a Copernican revolution. The experienced world is a joint product of mind-independent matter and mind-imposed form.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Binding is the work of the understanding and is presupposed by every perception. Against Hume, who found no impression of a self and called the mind a bundle of perceptions, Kant argues that unity cannot be an item within experience because it is what makes connected experience possible.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Intuitions come through sensibility and concepts come from the understanding. Cognition arises only when the two are combined in a synthesis that a single self-consciousness can own.
core_claims_and_evidence: Objects of experience are appearances, empirically real but transcendentally ideal, while things in themselves remain unknowable.
Space and time are a priori forms of intuition contributed by the subject, and time conditions all representations, inner and outer.
Unified experience requires that ‘I think’ can accompany all of one's representations.
In the Paralogisms, Kant argues that proofs of a simple, identical, immortal soul slide fallaciously from the formal unity of the ‘I think’ to claims about a substance.
In the Refutation of Idealism, Kant argues that consciousness of one's existence in time presupposes perception of persisting objects in space.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Judged as a theory of consciousness in today's sense, Kant leaves phenomenal character unexplained and never poses the hard problem. His terminology invites confusion, because his ‘phenomena’ are appearances as opposed to things in themselves and have nothing directly to do with phenomenal consciousness in the Nagel–Block sense.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Kant holds that the mind, like everything else, is known only as appearance, so what consciousness is in itself is unanswerable in principle. This limit has led to arguments that Kant belongs in the Challenge category as the founding ancestor of mysterianism.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a theory of the conditions of possible experience, which sits one level above the first-order ontologies the Landscape sorts. Kant separates his view from Berkeley's subjective idealism, holding that empirical objects are fully real and only their form depends on the mind.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Kant's conditions for experience are formal (synthesis and unified apperception), not tied to any material, but the subject in itself is unknowable, so the view gives no verdict on machines.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: The Paralogisms dismantle proofs that the soul is an immortal substance, but since the self in itself is unknowable, theoretical reason cannot rule survival out either.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Since knowledge is limited to appearances, questions of ultimate purpose lie beyond what Kant's theory of cognition can settle.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Kant's account says nothing about what the subject is in itself, so it cannot say whether a copy would preserve it.
